errors.unsupportedFormat: EmuDome can't open .{ext} files. Choose a GBA game (.gba, .gb, .gbc).
errors.consoleNotYet: {console} support arrives in Phase {phase}. For now, open a GBA game.
errors.coreNotFound: Core {file} not found. Run scripts/fetch-cores (see the README) or set EMUDOME_CORES_DIR.
errors.coreDamaged: Core {file} is not the one EmuDome ships, so it was not loaded. Reinstall EmuDome.
errors.openFailed: Couldn't open the game. Check that the file is a working GBA game. Details: {detail}
errors.coreIncompatible: The emulator for this console could not be started. Reinstall EmuDome. Details: {detail}
errors.romUnreadable: Couldn't read the game file. Check that it is still there and that its drive is connected. Details: {detail}
errors.coreRefusedGame: The emulator could not run this game. Check that the file is a complete, working copy of the game.
errors.coreNeedsRestart: A game on the {core} core stopped answering. Restart EmuDome to open games on this core again.
errors.noGame: No game is open. Open one first.
errors.appClosing: EmuDome is closing. Open the game again when it starts.
errors.nativeVideoUnavailable: Native video isn't available on this system. Keep using “In the webview”.
errors.webviewBackgroundFailed: Couldn't change the interface background: {detail}. Try again.
errors.slotEmpty: Slot {slot} is empty. Save to it first.
errors.stateSaveFailed: Couldn’t save to slot {slot}: {detail}. Check that the save folder is writable.
errors.stateLoadFailed: Couldn’t read slot {slot}: {detail}. Try again or use another slot.
errors.stateInvalid: The state in slot {slot} doesn’t fit this game or this core version. Save it again.
errors.settingUnknown: Unknown setting: it is ignored. If it keeps happening, export the log from Settings › About.
errors.settingLevelRefused: This setting only applies to {levels}: change it there.
errors.settingInvalidValue: Invalid value for “{name}”: back to the default.
errors.settingsWriteFailed: Couldn’t save the settings: check the free disk space and try again.
errors.settingsReadFailed: Couldn’t read the settings file, so the change wasn’t saved and the file was left as it is. Check that the drive is connected and the file can be opened, then try again.
errors.libraryFolderUnreachable: The folder {path} can’t be reached: the drive may be disconnected. Reconnect it or choose another folder.
errors.libraryGameUnknown: This game is no longer in the library. Search for games again from the library.
errors.libraryGameUnavailable: The game file can’t be found any more. Reconnect the drive or add its folder again.
errors.libraryWriteFailed: Couldn’t save the library: check the free disk space and try again.
errors.libraryReadFailed: Couldn’t read the library file, so the change wasn’t saved and the file was left as it is. Check that the drive is connected and the file can be opened, then try again.
errors.coverInvalid: This image can’t be opened. Choose a JPG or PNG file.
errors.undoFailed: Couldn’t go back to before the load: {detail}. Load another quick save.
errors.saveUnreadable: The in-game save can’t be read, so EmuDome set it aside. Restore a backup from Saves.
errors.saveGameOpen: This game is open. Close it and try again.
errors.saveImportInvalid: This file isn’t a save EmuDome can import ({detail}). Choose a .sav, .dsv or .duc file.
errors.saveFileFailed: Couldn’t use the save file: {detail}. Check that the saves folder is writable and try again.
errors.gameUnidentified: This file isn’t a game EmuDome can recognise: its header doesn’t match its console. Check that it’s a complete, working dump. Details: {detail}
errors.savesMigrationFailed: Couldn’t move your old saves to their new place. Nothing was lost: they stay where they were and EmuDome tries again at the next start. Details: {detail}
errors.savesMigrationIncomplete: Your saves moved to their new place, but {left} old files couldn’t be matched to one game for sure and stayed where they were. See the list in {report}.
errors.screenshotFailed: Couldn’t save the screenshot: {detail}. Check that the saves folder is writable and try again.
errors.effectNotLoaded: Couldn’t use the effect “{name}”, so the game shows without it. Choose another effect or another file.
errors.biosUnreadable: Couldn’t read this file: {detail}. Check that it’s still there and choose it again.
errors.biosWrongSize: This file doesn’t have the right size for this row. Choose the right file.
errors.biosOtherSlot: This file belongs to another row of this page. Choose it there.
errors.biosFileFailed: Couldn’t save EmuDome’s copy of the file: {detail}. Check the free disk space and try again.
errors.biosDsiFilesMissing: DSi mode needs your DS and DSi system files, so the game runs as a DS. Add them in Settings › BIOS and firmware.
errors.biosDsMenuFilesMissing: Starting from the DS menu needs your DS system files, so the game starts directly. Add them in Settings › BIOS and firmware.
errors.nativeVideoFallback: Native video couldn’t start ({detail}), so the game shows in the interface instead. You can keep playing; update your graphics driver and restart EmuDome to try again.
errors.videoSurfaceFailed: Couldn’t draw on the screen ({detail}), so the game isn’t shown. Switch to another app and back, or restart EmuDome.
errors.audioUnavailable: No sound: the audio output can’t be used ({detail}). EmuDome keeps trying; check that speakers or headphones are connected.
errors.controllersUnavailable: Controllers can’t be used this time ({detail}). Use the keyboard, or restart EmuDome to try again.
errors.threadStopped: Part of EmuDome stopped after an internal error ({thread}). Save from the quick menu if you can, then restart EmuDome.

scale.name: Image size
scale.desc: Whole pixels keeps every pixel the same size and leaves borders at the sides.

aspect.name: Aspect ratio
aspect.desc: Use the console’s original proportions or force others.

filter.name: Pixel smoothing
filter.desc: How much to soften the pixels when the image is enlarged.

surround.name: Background around the game
surround.desc: What you see in the empty space when the game does not fill the screen.

optionDesc.cover: A gradient taken from the cover
optionDesc.blur: The game enlarged and blurred. Computer only
optionDesc.image: A photo or picture from your files

surroundImg.name: Background image
surroundImg.desc: JPG or PNG; fits the screen.

surroundDim.name: Darken the background
surroundDim.desc: A darker background distracts less from the game.

surroundAnim.name: Animated background
surroundAnim.desc: The gradients move slowly. Off when “Reduce motion” is on.

fps.name: Show frames per second (FPS)
fps.desc: A counter in a corner of the screen. Shortcuts: F9 on the keyboard, L3 + X on the controller.

window.name: Window mode
window.desc: How EmuDome opens on the computer.

winsize.name: Window size
winsize.desc: Exact multiples of the console resolution, or free.

portrait.name: Game position in portrait
portrait.desc: Where to put the game when you hold the phone upright.

orient.name: Screen orientation
orient.desc: Lock the phone in portrait or landscape for this game.

path.name: Display method
path.desc: Accelerated is faster and needed for screen effects. Choose Compatible if the screen stays black or the menu does not appear over the game.

vsync.name: Vertical sync (V-Sync)
vsync.desc: Removes tearing lines from the image. May add a little input delay.

api.name: Graphics API
api.desc: Change it only if you see image problems. Applies the next time the game starts.

res3d.name: Resolution of 3D games
res3d.desc: Sharper 3D games. Needs a more powerful graphics card.

texf.name: Texture filter
texf.desc: Smooths or redraws the textures of Nintendo 3DS games.

fxpick.name: Screen effect
fxpick.desc: Shows at once on the paused game. Needs the Accelerated display method.

optionDesc.lcd: Thin lines like on the Game Boy Advance
optionDesc.lcd_grid: Every pixel apart, as seen up close
optionDesc.file: The .slangp file you chose in “Add an effect from a file”

fxint.name: Strength
fxint.desc: How visible the effect is over the image.

fxbright.name: Brightness
fxbright.desc: Makes up for the darkening caused by the effect.

fxfile.name: Add an effect from a file
fxfile.desc: Effects in RetroArch format (.slangp) that you downloaded yourself.

cycle.name: Layouts to cycle through
cycle.desc: The ones you step through with the shortcut or the quick menu, in this order.

custom.name: Free layout
custom.desc: Drag and resize the two screens wherever you want.

ratio.name: Screen size ratio
ratio.desc: How large the main screen is compared with the other.

gap.name: Gap between screens
gap.desc: Quick choice: “Like on the DS” uses the real distance.

rot.name: Rotation
rot.desc: For games you hold like a book.

swap.name: Swap screens
swap.desc: How the button that swaps the two screens behaves.

second.name: Second screen on another monitor
second.desc: Shows the bottom screen on a second connected monitor.

stereo.name: Stereoscopic 3D
stereo.desc: The Nintendo 3DS 3D effect on a normal screen.

vol.name: Volume
vol.desc: Game volume, separate from the system volume.

ff.name: Sound in fast forward
ff.desc: What you hear while the game runs faster.

mic.name: Microphone (Nintendo DS and 3DS)
mic.desc: For games that ask you to blow or speak. The real microphone asks for permission.

lat.name: Latency
lat.desc: Low responds sooner; Safe avoids crackling on slow devices.

spstart.name: Speed at start
spstart.desc: The speed every game starts at.

ffmode.name: Fast forward on the keyboard
ffmode.desc: How the Tab key works. On the controller: hold L3 + R2, or L3 + up to turn it on and off.

ffval.name: Fast-forward speed
ffval.desc: “Maximum” goes as fast as the device can.

slow.name: Slow motion
slow.desc: Speed when slow motion is on.

rew.name: Rewind while held
rew.desc: Backspace on the keyboard, hold L3 + L2 on the controller. Experimental on the Nintendo 3DS.

rewlen.name: How far you can rewind
rewlen.desc: More seconds use more of the device’s memory.

runahead.name: Reduce input delay (run-ahead)
runahead.desc: Computes frames ahead for a quicker response. Uses more processor.

autoq.name: Auto quick save
autoq.desc: A slot EmuDome updates by itself while you play.

autoexit.name: Auto quick save on close
autoexit.desc: So you can pick up exactly where you left off.

resume.name: When a game starts
resume.desc: What to do when you open a game you have played before.

undo.name: Allow undoing a load
undo.desc: Keeps your game aside before every load.

backups.name: Backups of the in-game save
backups.desc: How many earlier copies to keep, to go back if something goes wrong.

rtc.name: Game’s internal clock
rtc.desc: For games that use the date and time (events, seasons).

import.name: Import saves from other emulators
import.desc: DeSmuME (.dsv), Action Replay backups (.duc) and .sav files.

savedir.name: Saves folder
savedir.desc: Where EmuDome keeps saves and quick saves on this device.

ab.name: A/B layout
ab.desc: Like on Nintendo: A is the right button. As printed: A is the button labelled A.

remap.name: Button remapping
remap.desc: Choose which button does what, for all games, for a console or for one game.

turbo.name: Repeated press (turbo)
turbo.desc: Buttons that repeat by themselves while you hold them.

mod.name: Shortcut button
mod.desc: Hold it and press another button to save, load or change speed.

lid.name: Close and open the lid
lid.desc: For Nintendo DS and 3DS games that ask you to close the console.

dead.name: Stick dead zone

stickdpad.name: Use the left stick as the D-pad
stickdpad.desc: Past this point the stick counts as the D-pad.

trig.name: Trigger threshold
trig.desc: How far to press the analogue triggers for them to count.

rumble.name: Vibration
rumble.desc: For games that use the Rumble Pak.

gyro.name: Gyroscope
gyro.desc: For Nintendo 3DS games you control by tilting the console.

pointer.name: Touching the bottom screen
pointer.desc: How to touch the DS and 3DS bottom screen.

confirm.name: Confirm button in menus
confirm.desc: Only for EmuDome menus, not for games.

repeat.name: Button repeat in menus
repeat.desc: How soon a held button starts repeating.

tedit.name: Customise touch controls
tedit.desc: Move and resize the buttons over the paused game.

tport.name: Portrait layout
tport.desc: The one used when you hold the phone upright.

tland.name: Landscape layout
tland.desc: The one used when you hold the phone sideways.

tskin.name: Button look
tskin.desc: Style of the touch buttons, including the ones you import.

topac.name: Opacity
topac.desc: How visible the buttons are over the game.

thapt.name: Vibration on touch
thapt.desc: A small vibration on every press.

thide.name: Hide the buttons after
thide.desc: They come back as soon as you touch the screen.

tpad.name: Hide when a controller is connected
tpad.desc: The buttons come back if you disconnect the controller.

lang.name: Language
lang.desc: EmuDome’s language. Games keep their own language.

theme.name: Theme
theme.desc: Black turns pixels off on OLED screens.

accent.name: Accent colour
accent.desc: The colour of main buttons and of the selection.

ui.name: Interface
ui.desc: TV mode uses large text and is driven with the controller. Automatic turns it on in full screen with a controller connected.

start.name: When EmuDome starts, open
start.desc: What you see when you open the app.

bgpause.name: Pause when EmuDome is in the background
bgpause.desc: The game stops if you switch to another window or app.

confirmdel.name: Ask before deleting
confirmdel.desc: For saves, slots and games on Google Drive.

updates.name: EmuDome updates
updates.desc: On Android, updates come from the Play Store.

folders.name: Game folders
folders.desc: EmuDome looks for games in these folders on this device.

scanstart.name: Look for new games at start
scanstart.desc: Checks the folders every time you open EmuDome.

watch.name: Add new games right away
watch.desc: Watches the folders while EmuDome is open.

group.name: Group by console
group.desc: Splits the library into sections by console.

region.name: Preferred region for names
region.desc: When a game has different names in different regions.

hidden.name: Hidden games
hidden.desc: Games you removed from the library without deleting them.

covers.name: Generated covers
covers.desc: The style used for games without an image of yours.

option.rom_icon: Game icon when there is one

acct.name: Google account
acct.desc: {name} · EmuDome only sees the files it uploads to Google Drive.

squick.name: Quick saves

ssettings.name: Settings
ssettings.desc: Device-specific ones stay on that device.

sgames.name: Games on Google Drive
sgames.desc: Upload a game to download it on your other devices.

sauto.name: Automatic sync
sauto.desc: Downloads before a game starts and uploads when you close it.

option.game: When each game starts and closes

swifi.name: Wi-Fi only

textsize.name: Text size
textsize.desc: Enlarges EmuDome’s text, not the games’.

toggle.name: Toggle instead of hold
toggle.desc: For fast forward, rewind and repeated press.

cblind.name: Colour-blind filter on the game

settingsUi.title: Settings
settingsUi.scopeRegion: Which games the changes apply to

scope.globalSub: The starting value for every game

scope.consoleLine: You change only {console} games. Settings with a dot differ from “All games”; the others follow it.
scope.gameLine: You change only {title}. Settings with a dot differ from its console’s games; the others follow them.

settingsUi.notYet: This arrives in a future update.
settingsUi.emptyOnly: No settings changed here. Every value is inherited.

intro.bios: EmuDome works without these files thanks to free replacements already built in. If you copied the files from your console, you can use them for the best compatibility.
intro.advanced: For those who want to go further. Change the engine options only if you know what they do: the ones marked “at the next start” apply when you reopen the game.

empty.title: No saves yet
empty.text1min: When you play, EmuDome saves automatically every minute and when you close the game. You make quick saves from the quick menu or with {combo}.
empty.text5min: When you play, EmuDome saves automatically every 5 minutes and when you close the game. You make quick saves from the quick menu or with {combo}.
empty.textNever: When you play, EmuDome saves automatically when you close the game. You make quick saves from the quick menu or with {combo}.
empty.formats: Also from DeSmuME and other emulators: .sav, .dsv, .duc

importer.title: Import a save
importer.intro: From DeSmuME, an Action Replay backup or another emulator. Before importing, EmuDome makes a backup of the current save.

format.actionReplay: {file} · recognised as an Action Replay backup

importer.gameNone: Choose the game this save belongs to.
importer.replaceWarn: This game already has a save ({when}). It will be replaced; the current version stays among the backups.
importer.formats: Formats: DeSmuME (.dsv), Action Replay (.duc), .sav files from other emulators. To export a save, choose the game and use “Export…”.

conflict.title: Two versions of the same save
conflict.text: {title} was saved on two devices since the last sync. Choose which one to use: the other stays among the backups.
conflict.later: Decide later, open this device’s version

welcome.title: Welcome to EmuDome
welcome.lead: Your Game Boy, Game Boy Advance, Nintendo DS and Nintendo 3DS games, in one app, on computer and phone.

games.title: Where do you keep your games?
games.lead: Choose one or more folders. EmuDome reads the games from there, without moving or copying them.
games.background: You can go ahead: the search goes on in the background.

controller.title: Set up the controller
controller.lead: {name} connected. How do you want the A and B buttons?
controller.nintendo: A is the right button, as on the original consoles. Recommended.
controller.printed: A is the button with the letter A, at the bottom.
controller.press: Press a button to try it.
controller.pressed: Press a button to try it: you pressed {which}, in the game it is {button}.
controller.unused: Press a button to try it: you pressed {which}, the game does not use it.

ready.driveDesc: Copy saves and settings to all your devices
